text:
Anika (PM): quick check — Q3 prioritization: should we shift weight from growth metrics to reliability/launch gates? have two customer-driven asks that are colliding with throughput work.

Leo (Eng): curious which asks.

Anika (PM): 1) Adaptive batching (improves cost/throughput; reduces token cost ~20%) — medium effort. 2) Private VPC (enterprise security req from 3 deals) — high effort but direct revenue.

Ethan (Sales): note: 2 large deals are contingent on Private VPC. combined ARR ~ $350k/year if we ship in H2.

Maya (Data): rough RICE calcs I threw together. see below.

Maya (Data): ```
Feature | Reach | Impact | Confidence | Effort (sprints) | RICE
Adaptive batching | 100k req/day | 2.5 | 0.7 | 3 | 583
Private VPC | 10 accounts | 4.0 | 0.6 | 8 | 75
```

Carlos (Ops): PVPC has infra/service implications: networking, audit logs, KMS. effort might be 10+ sprints if we include on-prem options.

Olga (Design): PVPC also needs admin UX and onboarding flows — not trivial.

Leo (Eng): agree with Carlos. If effort is 10, RICE drops a lot. Also adaptive batching has infra risk but mostly runtime work which we can prototype in a sprint.

Anika (PM): so tradeoff: high immediate ARR vs platform efficiency that benefits many customers and reduces future costs. Thoughts on gating and launch criteria?

Ethan (Sales): for PVPC, customers require: SOC2 + VPC peering + KMS. They expect pilot in 3 months. If we ask them to wait, deal slips.

Maya (Data): proposal: reweight RICE temporarily for Q3 to emphasize "revenue impact / sales-blocking" as higher impact. But keep a separate slot for efficiency bets.

Leo (Eng): operational sanity: we can't just reprioritize without adjusting scope. If PVPC is top, we should scope it into a minimal MVP: VPC peering + audit logs + customer-managed keys. defer on-prem/air-gapped. That might get timeline to ~6 sprints.

Anika (PM): suggested launch gates for PVPC MVP: 1) internal security review signoff, 2) pilot with single customer, 3) e2e sandbox with KMS. If pass -> green.

Carlos (Ops): add SLO targets to gate: onboarding < 2 days for engineer, and audit retention >= 90 days.

Olga (Design): I'll sketch the pilot onboarding flow and sample admin console screens by next Tue.

Ethan (Sales): I'll lock the pilot customers to the MVP scope and push expectation management.

Maya (Data): if we temporarily bump PVPC score, we should also earmark a small team for adaptive batching exploratory work so we don't lose momentum.

Leo (Eng): we can do a 2-sprint spike on batching paired with PVPC MVP work. pairing reduces rework.

Anika (PM): decision proposal: prioritize PVPC MVP for Q3 with scoped gates; run adaptive batching spike and schedule full batching work for Q4 unless spike shows low effort. Vote? :thumbsup: = PVPC priority, :thumbsdown: = keep batching top.

Olga (Design): :+1:

Ethan (Sales): :+1: (customers locked to MVP)

Leo (Eng): :+1: if we scope and do batching spike

Carlos (Ops): :+1: with the SLOs added

Maya (Data): :+1: but please update RICE sheet and record new weights (revenue multiplier x1.5 this quarter).

Anika (PM): thanks — I'll update the roadmap doc, adjust RICE weights for Q3, and post new launch gates. pinging prod-bot to create a follow-up ticket.

prod-bot: Created ticket #PRD-4826 "PVPC MVP — Q3 launch gates" assigned to Anika, Leo, Carlos. link: https://redwood.internal/PRD-4826

Anika (PM): will share revised RICE spreadsheet and the gate checklist in this thread tomorrow.

Ethan (Sales): heads up: customers expect NDA + data processing agreement before pilot. adding legal checklist to the ticket.

Leo (Eng): scheduling spike now. thanks everyone.
